clue.text: One who follows another about in a branch of learning

indicators.note: about means going round, so the follower's word is placed around the next piece

parts.note: a disciple is a follower of a teacher or leader
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who trails after a mentor within an academic field.
explanation.definitionFit: A discipline is a field of study, such as history or chemistry, taught and researched as a subject.

clue.text: I stood for office in Middle-Eastern country

parts.note: taken as written
to run is to stand as a candidate in an election

explanation.surface: Someone recalls being a candidate in an election somewhere in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation of the Middle East, formerly called Persia, with Tehran as its capital.

clue.text: Credit note gets money for a fool

parts.note: CR is the usual abbreviation for credit on a statement
E is one of the musical notes A to G
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: A bank's credit slip turns into cash for a gullible person.
explanation.definitionFit: Cretin is an insulting word for a stupid person, a synonym of idiot or dolt.

clue.text: Explorer, one given all-round support

indicators.note: all-round says the support word goes right round the other piece

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge or arch
taken as written

explanation.surface: An adventurer who is backed up on every side.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is one of the first people to explore or settle a new region, an early explorer.

clue.text: Is a vote in the affirmative, producing a surprised reaction

parts.note: taken as written
aye (also spelt ay) is a yes vote, as in parliament's 'the ayes have it'

explanation.surface: A yes vote prompts someone's startled response.
explanation.definitionFit: 'I say!' is a dated British exclamation of surprise or mild shock, like 'goodness!'.

clue.text: Competitor in an event ran terribly

indicators.note: in says the answer is found inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A runner in some race performed very badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Competitor in an event' looks like the whole definition, but 'in' signals the letters to be found within 'event ran terribly'; 'an' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrant is someone who has entered a contest, so a competitor taking part.

clue.text: Chart showing relative positions

parts.note: reads like a diagram of where things stand, but 'relative' means family members and 'positions' their places in the line of descent

explanation.surface: A diagram that maps how things are placed against one another.
explanation.definitionFit: A family tree is a diagram of a family's relatives across generations, showing each member's place in it.

clue.text: A gamekeeper might, if the bag isn't good enough

definitions.text: A gamekeeper might, if the bag isn't good enough

parts.words: A gamekeeper might, if the bag isn't good enough
parts.note: a shooting party's bag is the game shot; a keeper whose bag is poor could be fired, an idiom about a sack

explanation.surface: A gamekeeper whose day's haul of birds is disappointing faces consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the sack is a British idiom for being dismissed from a job, here punning on the bag of game.

clue.text: It hinges on the number of spectators attending

definitions.meaning: an entrance barrier that swings on hinges in a fence or wall
the attendance figure at a sporting fixture

explanation.definitionFit: A gate swings on hinges, and a match's gate is the crowd count or the takings from it.

clue.text: Robust shoes will be

definitions.meaning: shoes are shaped on a cobbler's last, a foot-shaped model

explanation.definitionFit: Made to last means built durably, and shoes are literally made on a last, a cobbler's form.

clue.text: One's getting in support to carry on the fight

indicators.note: getting in says one piece enters the middle of another

parts.note: a rest is a prop or support, as for a snooker cue
I is the Roman numeral one, and 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A person enlisted as a backer to keep up a struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to fight against something and keep opposing it, so to continue the struggle.

clue.text: Impressed by a stockholder perhaps

parts.note: sounds like being awed by a shareholder, but means marked with a hot iron by an owner of livestock

explanation.surface: Someone who was awed by a major shareholder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle are branded, marked with a hot iron, by the rancher who owns the stock.

clue.text: Boy upset at vandalised tourist attraction

indicators.note: vandalised means smashed up, so the letters of the words before are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A lad is distressed at a sightseeing site that has been damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'vandalised' rearranges all ten letters of 'Boy upset at'.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty spot is a scenic place that visitors go to admire, so a tourist attraction.

clue.text: Too proud to take lodgers, honest!

parts.note: to be above something is to consider it beneath one
to board people is to house them as paying lodgers

explanation.surface: A landlady too proud to let rooms protests that she is straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Above board means open and legitimate, with nothing concealed, so honest.

clue.text: Attractive girl easily caught in the field

definitions.meaning: a dated word for a pretty young woman
in cricket a ... catch is a simple one for a fielder

explanation.definitionFit: Dolly is old slang for a pretty girl, and in cricket an easy catch is called a dolly.

clue.text: Break down in the course of an investigation

definitions.text: Break down in the course of an investigation

parts.words: Break down in the course of an investigation
parts.note: sounds like collapsing under questioning, but means separating something into parts to study it

explanation.surface: A suspect cracks during police questioning.
explanation.definitionFit: To analyse is to break something down into its components to examine it closely, as investigators do.

clue.text: Wakes all awry

indicators.note: all, as in 'all over the place', says the letters of the word are scattered

explanation.surface: Someone's funeral vigils have gone completely wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Askew means crooked or out of line, a close synonym of awry.

clue.text: Rod, pole or perch

parts.note: looks like a list of old units of length, each equal to five and a half yards, but each is also something a bird settles on

explanation.surface: Three names for the same old measure of length.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a perch or rail where birds settle to rest, like a pole or rod.

clue.text: Eager to obtain grand ring set in silver

indicators.note: set in says the pieces are mounted inside the next, as a stone in a setting

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
G is short for grand, a thousand
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Keen to buy a fine ring mounted in silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly excited and impatient, keen to see or hear something.

clue.text: Live on a range

parts.note: to be is to exist or live, so 'are' as in 'they are'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lives out on open grazing land.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a range or extent, as in an area of expertise or a range of territory.

clue.text: Strips, being about to get some rest

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for strips is read backwards

parts.note: peels are strips of rind, and to peel is to strip

explanation.surface: Undressing before getting some rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleep is the body's natural rest each night, so a period of repose.

clue.text: Drinks up with a companion and leaves

indicators.note: in a down light, up says the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: nips are small measures of spirits
taken as written
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Someone finishes their drinks with a friend and goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green vegetable, eaten as its leaves.

clue.text: Throw out a proposed scheme

explanation.definitionFit: To project is to throw or cast forward, and a project is a planned piece of work.

clue.text: Pray the change will do you good

indicators.note: change says the letters of the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice that praying and a fresh start will benefit you.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: treatment is something that will do you good.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is treatment meant to heal or improve health, something that benefits the patient.

clue.text: Knew cry comes from a woodpecker

indicators.note: comes from says the answer is made out of the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Someone recognised the call of a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The wryneck is a small bird of the woodpecker family, named for twisting its neck.

clue.text: Thought it will turn up in time

indicators.note: in places the turned piece inside the word for a time

parts.note: noon is the time of midday

indicators.note: in a down light, turn up says the word is read upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a lost item will reappear eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is an idea or belief, something thought.

clue.text: Spinners put back on, being very accurate

indicators.note: put back says the word is written backwards

parts.note: tops are toys that spin
taken as written

explanation.surface: Replacing the bowlers makes the attack precise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinners' suggests cricket's spin bowlers, but they are toy tops.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on is British slang for exactly right, perfectly accurate.

clue.text: Flag with a tale of heroism

parts.note: to flag is to tire or droop, like to sag
taken as written

explanation.surface: A banner bearing an epic story of courage.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long story of heroic deeds, originally the Norse and Icelandic prose epics.

clue.text: It develops in East and breaks round West

definitions.text: It develops in East and breaks round West

parts.words: It develops in East and breaks round West
parts.note: reads like a weather system, but describes daybreak: light comes up in the east and spreads westwards

explanation.surface: A weather front forms in the east and sweeps round to the west.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is the first light of day, rising in the east; dawn is said to break.

clue.text: Involved in a row, Rosa is upset

indicators.note: upset says the letters of the name are tipped over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Rosa is distressed after getting caught up in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a quarrel; it means rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Oars are the blades pulled when you row a boat, so they are what is used in rowing.

clue.text: Encouraging a number to take part in audition

indicators.note: take part in says the number goes into the middle of the other word

parts.note: audition is the sense of hearing
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A hopeful sign that a group will perform at a tryout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' suggests a tryout, but it is the faculty of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartening means cheering and giving courage, so encouraging.
